name: Northern Portugal
summary: A river city, a green wine valley, and Portugal's only national park. April is mild, the waterfalls are full, and you never need Lisbon.
why: It is the relaxed European alternative: beautiful, cultural, and easier to pace than Italy or Spain's famous cities. The 6-year-old can do boats, short trails and a city of tiles. The older two get the river terraces and the park.
distinctive: Terrace vineyards falling into a deep river, and a granite mountain park with spring waterfalls an hour or two from a real city.
weather: April in northern Portugal is mild, often the high teens, with some rain and green hills. The Douro can be warmer in the afternoon. The Atlantic is still cool for swimming. Seasonal expectation, not a forecast.
crowds: Porto's riverfront has visitors in April and is calmer than summer. The Douro quintas and Gerês trails are the quiet part. Easter 2027 is over by 29 March, so a mid-April trip misses Holy Week.
natureExperiences: A Douro boat between the terraces
Peneda-Gerês waterfalls and a short trail
The Atlantic at a river mouth, for walking
Porto's gardens as the rest day
age6: The river cruise, a short Gerês walk, and Porto's trams or a river-level promenade. Skip long granite scrambles.
age12: The boat, the park, and World of Discoveries or a similar hands-on museum if it is open.
age14: The same, plus how the terraces were built and a look at port wine from the outside of the process. Tasting is for adults.
adults: Porto on foot, a valley that is working farmland, and long lunches. This is the comfortable trip.
gettingAround: Train or metro in Porto. A car, ideally two, for the Douro and Gerês. Portugal drives on the right. The Douro train line is a scenic alternative for a day without the car, if the 2027 timetable still serves the village you choose.
meetingPoint: Porto. Bengaluru is usually one stop through Europe or the Gulf. Melbourne is the longer haul. Less painful than the Azores. Northern Spain is a different trip, not an add-on to this one.
visaAu: Schengen short-stay visa-free, EES biometrics on entry, ETIAS not yet operating at the time of research.
visaIn: Schengen visa, applied to Portugal if Portugal is the main stay.
disadvantages: The scenery is beautiful and less shocking than Fiordland, Cappadocia or Jiuzhaigou.
Gerês trails can be muddy and wet in April.
Right-hand driving is new for both families.
uncertainties: Which Gerês trails are suitable after spring rain in 2027.
Douro river-cruise dates. Many run in April. Confirm the operator.

image.alt: The Douro river between green terraces

gain: The easiest pleasant fortnight in Europe, with enough nature to honour the brief.
miss: A once-in-a-lifetime landscape, and a short flight from Melbourne.

cost.summary: Bengaluru to Porto is about ₹3.6–3.7 lakh for four adult typical returns. Melbourne is about ₹2.7 lakh at one recent fare and about ₹4.0 lakh at the past-year average, for three adults. Indian Schengen visa fees are about ₹35,000–₹40,000 before the visa-centre charge.

lines.text: Kayak.co.in’s typical return fare, Bengaluru to Porto, was ₹89,294–₹92,003 for one adult, with two stops. Four adult fares are about ₹3.6–3.7 lakh. A cheaper return was also seen recently, so the typical band is not the lowest fare on the page. Not an April 2027 quote.

Kayak.com.au’s past-year average return from Melbourne to Porto was about A$1,995. Three adult fares at that average are about ₹4.0 lakh. A Melbourne return found in the past five days was A$1,366, about ₹2.7 lakh for three. That is an average and one recent fare, not a typical low-to-high band. Not an April 2027 quote.

The Schengen consular fee is €90 from age 12 and €45 from age 6 until the 12th birthday. A German mission in India was collecting those fees as ₹9,900 and ₹5,000 on 1 October 2026. If the 6-year-old holds one of the four Indian passports, the four consular fees are about ₹35,000. If all four Indian passports are held by people aged 12 or over, they are about ₹40,000. The visa-centre service charge is extra. Australian passports pay no Schengen visa fee for a short stay.

cost.leftOut: Hotels, meals, the car, and international flights are not included.

stretch16: Add free days in the Douro. Do not add Lisbon and the Algarve.

days.experience: Land and walk the Ribeira once, then stop.
days.optional: A bookshop or a tile-fronted church, one only
days.highlight: A granite city stacked above a river
days.kids: The bridge view. No port-lodge crawl.
days.transfer: Porto airport is close to the city. The long haul is the tiring part.
days.wet: A covered market and an early night.

days.experience: A short river cruise and a garden.
days.optional: World of Discoveries if you want an indoor afternoon
days.highlight: Seeing the bridges from the water
days.kids: All three ages. Keep the cruise short.
days.transfer: On foot and by tram or metro.
days.seasonal: Confirm the boat is running in April.
days.wet: The museum becomes the main event.

days.experience: A free city day. One bakery, one viewpoint, one bookshop.
days.optional: A tram to the sea at Foz for a walk, not a swim
days.highlight: The Atlantic edge of the city
days.kids: The promenade. The water is cold.

days.experience: Drive or train into the Douro and stay three or four nights.
days.optional: A quinta visit aimed at the landscape, not a tasting session
days.kids: Window time. The valley roads twist. Motion-sickness pills if anyone needs them.
days.transfer: About 1.5–2 hours from Porto to Pinhão by car. The train is slower and more beautiful. Seven people may not fit one train plan with luggage. Two cars are simpler.
days.seasonal: April is green. Harvest crowds are in autumn.
days.wet: The drive is still worth it. Viewpoints from the car.

days.experience: A river boat between the terraces.
days.highlight: The valley from the water, which is calmer than the road
days.kids: All three. Sit together. Bring layers.
days.seasonal: Boats can cancel in high water or wind. Have a quintas-and-windows backup.
days.wet: A covered boat if one exists, or a manor-house visit.

days.experience: A free valley day. One viewpoint, a long lunch, a short walk.
days.kids: Drawing the terraces. A pool at the hotel if it has one.
days.seasonal: This is the heart of the relaxed pace.

days.experience: A second village or a train hop if the line is easy that day.
days.optional: Skip it and repeat the boat
days.highlight: How small the valley settlements are
days.seasonal: Do not try to see the whole Douro.

days.experience: Drive to the national park and do one short waterfall walk.
days.optional: A village spa with hot water
days.highlight: Granite, oak woods and spring water
days.kids: Choose the short trail. River rocks are slippery.
days.transfer: Gerês village is roughly 1.5–2 hours from the Braga side, and longer from deep in the Douro. Allow half a day to change base.
days.seasonal: April water is high, which is the reason to come, and the reason not to wade.
days.wet: A viewpoint from the road and the spa.

days.experience: Another short trail or a lake edge, then a free afternoon.
days.optional: Ponies only with a licensed handler who takes age 6
days.highlight: The only national park in the country, used gently
days.kids: All three on the easy path. No ridge walk.
days.wet: The interpretation centre if open, or back to Porto a day early.

days.experience: Return to Porto for the flight buffer.
days.optional: A last pastry and a river view
days.highlight: Leaving from the city you arrived in
days.transfer: About 1.5 hours from the Braga–Gerês side to Porto airport, longer from the park itself. Do not fly the same day you leave a trail.
days.seasonal: Build the buffer because Melbourne connections are unforgiving.
days.wet: Already indoors or in the car.
